findings.summary: Brackenridge-Tox outperforms Owlery-Enc on the three training platforms' test splits, with a mean paired difference of 2.1 macro-F1 points (95% CI [1.58, 2.69], p < 0.001, paired t-test, n=5 seeds).
findings.scope: Average macro-F1 over Gildcrest Forums, Nettlebank, and Pikestaff Chat test splits, 5 seeds.
findings.caveats: Significance is established only for this specific comparison and metric; no test is reported for per-subtype or Cobble-Board differences.

findings.summary: Brackenridge-Tox's advantage over Owlery-Enc does not clearly generalize to the unseen Cobble-Board platform: Brackenridge-Tox achieves 71.8 ± 0.9 macro-F1 vs 68.9 ± 1.1 for Owlery-Enc, but no statistical test is reported for this difference.
findings.caveats: Cobble-Board has no separate test partition; the difference is a mean difference only, not established as significant.

findings.summary: Brackenridge-Tox shows higher per-subtype F1 than Owlery-Enc on all four subtypes pooled over the training-platform test splits (e.g., identity attack: 70.2 vs 66.5; threat: 61.4 vs 58.9), but no statistical tests are reported for these differences.
findings.scope: Per-subtype F1 pooled over the three training-platform test splits, 5 seeds.
findings.caveats: No significance tests; differences are descriptive only.

findings.summary: Ablation shows that both contrastive pretraining and subtype heads contribute to Brackenridge-Tox's average macro-F1 on the training platforms: removing contrastive pretraining drops it from 81.9 to 80.6, removing subtype heads to 81.2, and removing both to 79.9.
findings.scope: Average macro-F1 over the three training-platform test splits, 5 seeds.
